2610.08303.title: Language Unalignability: Why Some Concepts Resist Cross-Cultural Benchmark Evaluation
2610.08303.paper_summary: Current evaluation of multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) rests on an implicit Translation-Isomorphism Assumption (TIA): that semantic structures across languages are congruent and mutually mappable without loss of information. We argue that this assumption is not merely violated in practice, but ill-posed in principle for a typologically identifiable class of concepts, including pragmatic markers, honorifics, and diachronically stratified terms. We formalize this failure using a usage-cloud framework, representing concepts as point sets of contextualized embeddings. We define $α$-unalignability as the impossibility of any mapping that simultaneously preserves lexical faithfulness (centroid correspondence) and structural faithfulness (local neighborhood topology). We provide three layers of evidence. Behaviorally, we show that FLORES-200 translation failures are predicted by language family and resource class but not by script, and that LOBSTER reasoning scores vary by family. Mechanistically, we report a Representation-Intervention Gap (RIG) in a nine-model case study on Yami: the models' activations encode a regularity along which Yami groups with other low-resource and Austronesian languages, yet interventions on language-specific neurons show no demonstrated advantage over random masks: the regularity is visible but not usable by this intervention. Finally, we operationalize these findings into a multidimensional diagnostic profile: Cycle-Consistency, Pragmatic-Load Disagreement, Manifold-Curvature Mismatch, and RIG. We argue that collapsing cultural competence into a single scalar incentivizes "probabilistic flattening," and that recognizing the unalignable class is a precondition for AI that respects, rather than erases, cultural divergence. This suggests that multilingual alignment is not a single well-defined objective, but a set of mutually incompatible projections.
2610.08303.paper_summary_zh: 目前對多語言大型語言模型（LLMs）的評估基於一個隱含的翻譯同構假設（TIA）：即語言之間的語義結構是一致的，且可以相互映射而不損失信息。我們認為這一假設不僅在實踐中被違反，從原則上來說，對於一類可識別的類型學概念（包括語用標記、敬語和歷時分層術語）來說是錯位的。我們使用使用雲框架對這一失敗進行形式化，將概念表示為上下文化嵌入的點集。我們定義$α$-不對齊性為同時保留詞彙忠實性（質心對應）和結構忠實性（局部鄰域拓撲）而無法進行任何映射。我們提供三層證據。在行為上，我們顯示FLORES-200翻譯失敗由語言家族和資源類別預測，而非由書寫系統預測，並且LOBSTER推理分數因家族而異。在機制上，我們報告了一個在Yami的九模型案例研究中的表徵干預差距（RIG）：模型的激活編碼了一種規律，根據該規律，Yami與其他低資源和南島語言分組，但對語言特定神經元的干預未顯示出相對於隨機掩碼的優勢：這一規律是可見的，但該干預無法使用。最後，我們將這些發現操作化為一個多維診斷檔案：循環一致性、語用負載不一致、流形曲率不匹配和RIG。我們認為將文化能力簡化為單一標量會激勵“概率平坦化”，並且認識到不可對齊的類別是尊重而非抹去文化差異的人工智能的前提條件。這表明多語言對齊不是一個單一的明確目標，而是一組相互不相容的投影。
2610.08303.author: Shu-Kai Hsieh et.al.
